text:
Predicates:
EatSalad(x) ::: x eats salads regularly.
Conscious(x) ::: x is very conscious about their health and eating habits.
HealthHome(x) ::: x grew up in a health-conscious childhood home.
NutritionalIntake(x) ::: x fulfills their nutritional daily intakes.
GoodRelationship(x) ::: x has a good relationship with their parents.
VisitGym(x) ::: x visits the gym at least once a day.
Taylor(x) ::: x is Taylor.
Premises:
∀x (EatSalad(x) → Conscious(x)) ::: All people who eat salads regularly are very conscious about their health and eating habits.
∀x (HealthHome(x) → EatSalad(x)) ::: All people who grew up in health-conscious childhood homes eat salads regularly.
∀x (NutritionalIntake(x) → HealthHome(x)) ::: All people who fulfill their nutritional daily intakes grew up in health-conscious childhood homes.
∀x (GoodRelationship(x) → NutritionalIntake(x)) ::: If people have good relationships with their parents, then they fulfill their nutritional daily intakes.
∀x (GoodRelationship(x) → ¬EatSalad(x)) ::: If people have good relationships with their parents, then they do not eat salads regularly.
∀x (VisitGym(x) → NutritionalIntake(x)) ::: If people visit the gym at least once a day, then they always fulfill their daily nutritional intakes.
(HealthHome(taylor) ∧ GoodRelationship(taylor)) ⊕ ¬(HealthHome(taylor) ∨ GoodRelationship(taylor)) ::: It is either both true that Taylor grew up in a health-conscious childhood home and she has a good relationship with her parents, or it is true that Taylor neither grew up in a health-conscious childhood home nor has a good relationship with her parents.
Conclusion:
EatSalad(taylor) ::: Taylor eats salads regularly.
